title: Stock Market Highlights, October 23: Sensex, Nifty extend losses as crude surges to $114, all sectors close in red - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights- Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 23rd October 2026.

The benchmark Nifty 50 fell 0.39% to 22,600, ‌and the Sensex shed 0.17% to 73,123.83.

The indexes lost 2.4% ‌and ⁠2.2% this week, respectively, with sentiment dampened by a ⁠rise in Brent crude oil futures to about $114 on energy supply fears after attacks on top exporter Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Houthis.

Fifteen of the 16 major sectors logged weekly losses. The broader small-caps and mid-caps underperformed benchmarks, losing 7.3% and 5.6% and posting their worst week in 20 months.

Find all the key highlights of Jio Platforms IPO Day 3 here

The currency ended 0.1% lower for the day at 94.9400, after depreciating by 0.4% on ‌Thursday. It was little changed for the week, after ‌rising ⁠1.4% last week.

SBI Card posts higher quarterly profit as asset quality improves, with lower provisions and steady credit growth.

HPCL shifts to delivered oil, using discounts from Middle East cargoes as freight costs spike amid Hormuz tensions.

Shriram Finance reported a 59 per cent year-on-year jump in second quarter net profit at Rs 3,677 crore against Rs 2,307 crore in the year ago quarter on the back of a healthy growth in net interest income and assets under management (AUM). AUM increased 17% YoY to ₹3,29,021.72 crore

Jubilant Pharmova plans about ₹1,400 crore rupee debt sale to fund capex and refinance overseas project liabilities.

Shree Cement Q2 profit dips 15% to ₹263.46 cr as revenue climbs 24%, powered by green energy and strong RMC growth.

India’s September crude imports rose 16% MoM to 22.26 MMT, with mixed changes in product exports and Russian volumes.

ATGL raises CNG prices by ₹4.45/kg due to higher LNG costs, reduced domestic gas and supply cuts, with regional rates shown in Ahmedabad, Faridabad, and Jalandhar.

India’s September crude imports rose 16% MoM to 22.26 MMT, with mixed changes in product exports and Russian volumes.

ATGL raises CNG prices by ₹4.45/kg due to higher LNG costs, reduced domestic gas and supply cuts, with regional rates shown in Ahmedabad, Faridabad, and Jalandhar.

LPG under-recovery at ₹327/cylinder in November; HPCL reports rising losses, debt refinances, and freight-linked costs in FY27.

Net profit: ₹409.09 crore for Q2 FY27; ₹717.37 crore for H1 FY27 (consolidated).

Strong financial performance: Consolidated Q2 revenue from operations rose to ₹3,801.54 crore from ₹2,922.79 crore a year earlier, while profit after tax increased from ₹284.44 crore to ₹409.09 crore. H1 revenue reached ₹7,082.35 crore and profit after tax ₹717.37 crore.

Board approved the unaudited Q2 and half-year results: The financial statements for the quarter and six months ended 30 September 2026 were approved following Audit Committee recommendation. The statutory auditor issued an unmodified limited-review conclusion.

Power transformer capacity expansion: CG Power approved ₹68 crore to add 10,000 MVA at its T3 power-transformer facility, which has 65,000 MVA existing capacity and is operating at 85% utilization. Completion is targeted in 12–15 months.

Major switchgear expansion programme: The Board approved approximately ₹300 crore for the S1 Ambad OIP facility to add 4,236 equivalent units annually; ₹15.31 crore for 3,600 additional EHV circuit breakers annually at S3 Unit-II; and an extra ₹9.45 crore for the GIS project in Nashik. These investments address capacity constraints and rising domestic and export demand.

Leadership and semiconductor expansion: Rajat Shah and Rushikesh Kulkarni were designated as Senior Management Personnel effective 23 October 2026. Separately, the group acquired 100% of Tosil Systems for ₹16.44 crore, adding VLSI and embedded-systems engineering capabilities to its semiconductor business.

Elgi Equipments announces a one-year window from Feb 2026 to Feb 2027 for transfer and dematerialization of physical shares sold before April 2019, in line with SEBI circular. Shareholders can submit documents via registrar KFintech. The window covers rejected or pending requests, mandatorily transfers shares in demat mode with a one-year lock-in, excluding disputes and IEPF transfers.

Adani Power reports record Q2 FY27 profit as demand-led volume growth and prior-period revenue recognition lift earnings

State Bank of India (SBI) on Friday said the recent cyber incident related to data leak has impacted a “very very” small number of customers and assured that customer balances are completely safe.

Honasa Consumer names Vipul Maheshwari CPTO to drive AI-led product and technology transformation across brands.

“Gold is having its toughest week in months. Spot prices are down more than 3.5% to around $4,015 an ounce, the lowest since July 20, and Thursday alone took off 2.8%. On MCX, December gold has slipped below ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams, more than 20% below this year’s peak of ₹1.81 lakh. Silver has broken below ₹2 lakh for the first time since December 2025.

Oil is driving this sell-off more than fear is. Brent is above $110 on fresh supply risks in the Gulf, and that has revived inflation worries. US data was already running hot, with September CPI at 3.7% and PPI at 6.3%. Markets now expect one more Fed hike before year-end. When rates are rising, an asset that pays no yield struggles, even when geopolitical risk is high.

In the near term, two events will set direction: the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting, where a pause is largely priced in, and next week’s PCE inflation data. $4,000-$3950 is the key support zone, and a clear break below it could extend the correction. The structural case is still intact, though. Central banks bought 289 tonnes in Q2 alone. For Indian investors, this is a time to add gradually, not to panic or chase.”

ITAT ruling: two connected flats can qualify as one residential house for LTCG exemption under Section 54F, subject to physical verification.
